raw_response:
My thinking:

I farm 10.1 mu here in Quzhou, same as most of my neighbors. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — that is how we have done it for many years. With just my wife and me at home, we manage most work ourselves, but hire the combine for harvest and the seeder.

For wheat this autumn, I will use an improved variety — Jimai or something similar that the seed shop recommends and that my neighbor planted last year with good results. I plant around October 10-15. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before plowing, about 50 kg per mu as base. Then top-dress urea at jointing in spring, about 20 kg per mu. That gives roughly 22 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K. I do not want to skimp — fertilizer is expensive but a thin wheat crop is worse. I plow with rotary tiller after maize comes off.

Irrigation: winter water before freeze, then jointing water, then grain-filling water. Three times usually. If spring is dry I add one more. My well works fine.

Pesticide: one spray for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, maybe a herbicide in spring for broadleaf weeds. Two applications usually enough.

Wheat yield I expect about 480-500 kg per mu. Last few years have been like this.

For maize after wheat in June, I direct-seed with no tillage — saves time and the ground is wet from wheat irrigation. Xianyu or Zhengdan hybrid seed, whatever the dealer has fresh. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at sowing, about 40 kg per mu, then top-dress urea at big flare stage, 25 kg per mu. So about 24 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K.

Maize I irrigate once or twice — at seedling if dry, and at tasseling. Usually two times.

Pesticide: one for armyworm/borer, sometimes one herbicide after sowing. Two applications.

Maize yield around 550-600 kg per mu if weather holds.
